title: Logarithmic Strain-Based Glen’s Flow Law for Glaciological Applications
content: This paper formulates a thermodynamically consistent finite-strain Maxwell–Glen model for glaciological applications in a Lagrangian setting. A multiplicative decomposition of the deformation gradient separates the elastic and viscous mappings, while a unit viscous Jacobian imposes isochoric creep. Viscous evolution is described by the material velocity gradient. Its trace-free constraint permits an exponential-map update that preserves the viscous Jacobian without a projection step. The elastic state is represented by the principal logarithm of the mixed elastic metric, and its work-conjugate material stress drives a Glen-type power law. Under the isotropic constitutive flow direction, the relevant tensors commute and the multiplicative metric update reduces to an additive elastic–viscous corrector. The matrix exponential is evaluated by a Cayley–Hamilton reduction valid for arbitrary, potentially nonsymmetric, three-dimensional arguments. A consistent linearisation supplies the material tangent for the finite-element equilibrium problem. Homogeneous simple shear verifies the invariant material pull-back under non-coaxial deformation, while a self-weighted plane-strain ice column confirms preservation of the viscous Jacobian to the solver tolerance.
